description:
## Why

People who write kernels will often have an agent write them. An agent that knows Elixir but not defk writes full Elixir in a kernel body (lists, maps, Enum pipelines, untyped arguments) and then fights the compile errors. usage_rules (added in defk-mob) is how an Elixir project collects its deps' rules into AGENTS.md or skills: a user lists `:defk` in their `usage_rules` config, runs `mix usage_rules.sync`, and their agent gets our rules. It reads `deps/defk/usage-rules.md` and `deps/defk/usage-rules/*.md`, so it works for git and path deps today, before any Hex release (gated on defk-sgw.5).

## What to ship

1. `usage-rules.md` at the repo root: short and dense, for an agent about to write or change a kernel:
   - what defk is for and when to stay in Elixir (the README's Elixir-first framing, in a few lines);
   - the subset at a glance: types and how arguments are declared, loops and for-collect, arrays and bitstrings, what is rejected and what to write instead;
   - testing: `Defk.Test.assert_agrees` and Elixir mode, run in both modes;
   - measuring before claiming a win (`Defk.Bench`, baselines), and where `Defk.Report` comes in;
   - reading a compile error: the code, and its entry in the compile-error catalogue.
2. Sub-rules in `usage-rules/` for the parts too long for the main file (a candidate split: `language.md`, `testing.md`, `measuring.md`), so users can inline the main rules and link the rest (`{:defk, sub_rules: :all, main: false, link: :markdown}`).
3. Possibly a pre-built skill in `usage-rules/skills/defk/SKILL.md` that users pull in with `package_skills: [:defk]`. Decide this in step 1 below. A skill loads only when its description matches, so its description must name concrete signals (`use Defk`, `defk` blocks, `Defk.Test`, a defk compile error code).

## Principles (from defk-djy)

- One source of truth. The rules are a condensed view of `docs/guides/cheatsheet.cheatmd`, `docs/language.md` and the `Defk.Errors` registry, not a parallel copy. Any list that `Defk.Errors` already holds (the rejected constructs and what to write instead, the planned and won't-do items) is generated the way `docs/scope.md`'s lists are, and a test fails when the files drift (like `test/scope_doc_test.exs`). Add the procedure to `docs/agents/generated-docs.md`.
- Every code example is checked, in both modes, by the same runner as the language doc examples (`test/language_doc_examples_test.exs`), and the links pass `test/docs_checks_test.exs`.
- Plain language, and honest about scope: say what defk is not yet and won't be, so an agent doesn't invent features.
- Short. Users inline these rules into their AGENTS.md, and every line costs context in someone else's project. Prune hard, and send the details to the guides with links that work outside the repo (the HexDocs URLs, as the compile-error links do since defk-djy.6).

## Steps

1. Decide the shape: what goes in the main file, which sub-rules exist, and whether we ship a skill. Record it as a "Choice (defk-XXX)" comment where the files are wired up, the way mix.exs does for the docs.
2. Write `usage-rules.md` and the sub-rules from the existing docs. Generate the parts that come from `Defk.Errors`.
3. Checks: examples in both modes, links, generated parts, all in `mix ci`.
4. Packaging: once mix.exs has a `package` config, include `usage-rules.md` and `usage-rules/` in `files:`. There is none yet, so leave a note at the docs config, or add `package` now with just `files:`.
5. Try it from outside: a scratch project with defk as a path dep and `usage_rules: [file: "AGENTS.md", usage_rules: [:defk]]`. Run `mix usage_rules.sync` and check what lands in its AGENTS.md (and in `.claude/skills` if we ship a skill).
6. Cold test (as in `docs/cold-tests/`): a fresh agent with only the synced rules writes and tests a small kernel (e.g. a checksum or count-min). Record where it went wrong and fix the rules. Write it up in `docs/cold-tests/`.

## Done when

- `usage-rules.md` (plus any sub-rules or skill) is in the repo, built from the existing docs, with its generated parts drift-checked.
- Every example runs in both modes and every link resolves, checked in `mix ci`.
- A scratch consumer's `mix usage_rules.sync` picks the rules up.
- A cold test with an agent that has only the rules is recorded, and the rules are fixed for what it found.
title: Ship a usage-rules.md for kernel authors (and their agents)
